latest.headline: Nine days out: Democrats hold 55 Senate seats after Colom's Mississippi upset, about 255 House seats, and 28 governorships with two still counting. Alaska decides the rest on Nov. 18.
lines: Senate: AP called Mississippi for Scott Colom (D) on Nov. 11. He beat Cindy Hyde-Smith by 5,605 votes. That's the eighth Democratic pickup and puts Democrats at 55, up from 47.
House: AP's count as of Nov. 9 was Democrats 255, Republicans 168, with 12 seats still uncalled. Democrats went in at 214.
Governors: Democrats flipped five (Georgia, Iowa, Nevada, Ohio and Texas) and lost none. Kansas and Alaska are still uncalled, and Democrats lead both.
Still out: Alaska Senate, governor and House (ranked-choice tabulation Nov. 18), Kansas governor (Holscher +7,479) and MN-01 (Johnson +321).

control: Senate: Democrats 55, Republicans 44, with Alaska uncalled. Going in it was 53R-47D. Democrats flipped Iowa, Kansas, Maine, Mississippi, North Carolina, Ohio, South Carolina and Texas and lost none. If Peltola holds Alaska, they'd have 56.
House: Democrats 255, Republicans 168 and 12 uncalled, per AP as of Nov. 9. Going in it was 218R-214D. The modern high-water mark is 257 Democratic seats in 2008, and that's in reach.
In the 54 battleground House seats we tracked, Democrats won 46 of the 52 called. They flipped 34 Republican seats. Republicans flipped one Democratic seat: ME-02, where Paul LePage won.
Governors: Democrats hold 28 called governorships, up from 24, with Kansas (D-held) and Alaska (R-held) uncalled. If they win both, they'd have 30.

On our desk: 117 calls. Every one that a network has since called went the same way. We pulled two calls on election night (Mississippi Senate and NV-02) and re-called NV-02 correctly once AP fixed its returns.
races: Mississippi Senate: Colom (D) 474,804, Hyde-Smith (R) 469,199, with 99% counted. AP called it Nov. 11 at about 3:05 PM MT. Our 10:02 PM election-night call for Hyde-Smith was wrong, and we retracted it at 11:03 PM.
CO-04: Eileen Laubacher (D) beat Rep. Lauren Boebert by 3,362 votes with 98% counted.
AZ-02: Eli Crane (R) held on against Jonathan Nez by 3,446 votes. AP called it Nov. 9.
ME-02: Paul LePage (R) beat Matt Dunlap by 5,420 votes. It's the only Democratic seat Republicans flipped in our battleground set.

Also called since our last update: Luna (FL-13), Salazar (FL-27), McGuire (VA-05) and Constantino (NY-21) for Republicans, and Taylor (VA-01), Knickerbocker (OH-10), Lacore (SC-01), Killin (CO-05), Shah (AZ-01) and Mendoza (AZ-06) for Democrats. All match our calls.
news: AP called Mississippi on Nov. 11, about a week after Election Day, once Colom's lead had grown from 1,138 votes to 5,605.
Alaska counts ballots through Nov. 17 and runs the ranked-choice tabulation on Nov. 18.
Louisiana's LA-05 and LA-06 go to Dec. 12 runoffs. Republicans are favored in both.
watch: Alaska Senate: Peltola (D) 121,487, Sullivan (R) 117,512, with 86% counted. That's a 3,975-vote lead with 9,526 votes for others, so the ranked-choice round could matter.
Alaska governor: Kreiss-Tomkins (D) is at 49.8%, just short of a majority. The three Republicans combined trail him. Ranked choice Nov. 18.
Alaska House: Begich (R) is at 49.0% in a four-way race. Ranked choice Nov. 18.

Kansas governor: Holscher (D) leads Masterson by 7,479 with 99% counted. AP hasn't called it, but we called it for Holscher on election night. Kansas has no automatic recount; a candidate can request one at their own cost.
MN-01: Jake Johnson (D) leads Rep. Brad Finstad (R) by 321 votes with 99% counted. That's inside Minnesota's automatic recount range of 0.5%.

20261104.headline: Democratic wave: Democrats take the Senate with at least 54 seats, are on track for about 240 to 250 House seats, and flip five governorships.
lines: Senate: Democrats have at least 54 seats on our calls, up from 47. They flipped seven Republican seats and lost none. Alaska and Mississippi are still uncalled, with Democrats narrowly ahead in both.
House: Democrats needed a net gain of 4. They flipped 27 Republican seats in the battleground races we've called and lost none. Our estimate is roughly 241 to 251 Democratic seats.
Governors: Democrats flipped Georgia, Iowa, Ohio, Texas and Nevada and have lost none so far. Kansas (Democratic-held) is still too close to call.
Still out: AK Senate (Peltola +626), MS Senate (Colom +43, recount likely), KS governor (Holscher +5,557), NV-02, the California House seats and a handful of close House races.

control: Senate, estimated: Democrats 54 to 56, Republicans 44 to 46. Going in it was 53R-47D. Democrats have 54 seats on our calls, and Alaska and Mississippi, where Democrats narrowly lead, would make 56.

Seven Democratic Senate pickups on our calls: Iowa (Turek), Kansas (Hamilton), Maine (Jackson over Collins), North Carolina (Cooper), Ohio (Brown), South Carolina (Andrews) and Texas (Talarico). Democrats lost no Senate seats.
House, estimated: Democrats about 241 to 251, Republicans about 183 to 193, and 1 independent. Going in it was 218R-214D. 218 is a majority.

How we got the House range: of 54 battleground seats we tracked, Democrats won 39 of the 42 called and lead in 10 of the 12 still counting. We assume the roughly 380 seats we didn't track stayed with the incumbent party, which is a conservative assumption in a wave this size. AP has not yet called House control.

Governors, estimated: Democrats 28 to 30, Republicans 20 to 22, up from 24 Democrats and 26 Republicans before the election. Flips: Georgia (Bottoms), Iowa (Sand), Ohio (Acton), Texas (Hinojosa) and Nevada (Ford). Still out: Kansas (Democratic-held) and Alaska (Republican-held, with the Democrat leading).
races: Texas: Talarico (D) leads Paxton by about 1.21 million with 96% counted, and Hinojosa (D) leads the governor's race by about 725,000.
Michigan Senate: El-Sayed (D) leads by about 335,000 with 97% counted, after Wayne County's late count.
Maine Senate: Jackson (D) beats Collins by about 49,000 with 86% counted.
Ohio: Brown (D) wins the Senate special by about 223,000, and Acton (D) wins governor by about 364,000.
Georgia: Ossoff (D) holds his Senate seat by about 754,000, and Bottoms (D) flips the governorship by about 360,000.
Minnesota: Klobuchar wins governor and Flanagan wins Senate after the Twin Cities vote closed early Republican leads.
news: Our desk made 102 calls (plus 7 overnight under the overnight rules) and was ahead of CNN on 71 of them. Typical lead: about 15 to 60 minutes on competitive races.
Mississippi Senate: we retracted our 10:02 PM call for Hyde-Smith after Colom took the lead. He's ahead by 43 votes with about 97% counted.
NV-02: we retracted our 1:21 AM call for Flippo (R) after AP revised the returns. Benitez-Thompson (D) now leads by about 18,900 with 86% counted.
Nevada results were missing from our CNN feed until about 1:20 AM MT.
watch: Alaska: about 74% counted. Peltola leads Sullivan by 626 votes. The governor and House leaders are just under 50%, so ranked-choice tabulation may decide them.
Mississippi Senate: Colom +43. The race is likely headed for a recount.
Kansas governor: Holscher +5,557 with 98% counted; Masterson needs about 63% of what's left.
California: CA-22 (Villegas +27,000, 57% counted) and CA-48 (von Wilpert +30,000, 52% counted). Late ballots usually lean Democratic.
Close House races: AZ-02, CO-04, CO-05, ME-02, MN-01, MT-01, NY-17 and NY-21. We update hourly today.

20261112.headline: Nine days out: Democrats hold 55 Senate seats after Colom's Mississippi upset, about 255 House seats, and 28 governorships with two still counting. Alaska decides the rest on Nov. 18.
lines: Senate: AP called Mississippi for Scott Colom (D) on Nov. 11. He beat Cindy Hyde-Smith by 5,605 votes. That's the eighth Democratic pickup and puts Democrats at 55, up from 47.
House: AP's count as of Nov. 9 was Democrats 255, Republicans 168, with 12 seats still uncalled. Democrats went in at 214.
Governors: Democrats flipped five (Georgia, Iowa, Nevada, Ohio and Texas) and lost none. Kansas and Alaska are still uncalled, and Democrats lead both.
Still out: Alaska Senate, governor and House (ranked-choice tabulation Nov. 18), Kansas governor (Holscher +7,479) and MN-01 (Johnson +321).

control: Senate: Democrats 55, Republicans 44, with Alaska uncalled. Going in it was 53R-47D. Democrats flipped Iowa, Kansas, Maine, Mississippi, North Carolina, Ohio, South Carolina and Texas and lost none. If Peltola holds Alaska, they'd have 56.
House: Democrats 255, Republicans 168 and 12 uncalled, per AP as of Nov. 9. Going in it was 218R-214D. The modern high-water mark is 257 Democratic seats in 2008, and that's in reach.
In the 54 battleground House seats we tracked, Democrats won 46 of the 52 called. They flipped 34 Republican seats. Republicans flipped one Democratic seat: ME-02, where Paul LePage won.
Governors: Democrats hold 28 called governorships, up from 24, with Kansas (D-held) and Alaska (R-held) uncalled. If they win both, they'd have 30.

On our desk: 117 calls. Every one that a network has since called went the same way. We pulled two calls on election night (Mississippi Senate and NV-02) and re-called NV-02 correctly once AP fixed its returns.
races: Mississippi Senate: Colom (D) 474,804, Hyde-Smith (R) 469,199, with 99% counted. AP called it Nov. 11 at about 3:05 PM MT. Our 10:02 PM election-night call for Hyde-Smith was wrong, and we retracted it at 11:03 PM.
CO-04: Eileen Laubacher (D) beat Rep. Lauren Boebert by 3,362 votes with 98% counted.
AZ-02: Eli Crane (R) held on against Jonathan Nez by 3,446 votes. AP called it Nov. 9.
ME-02: Paul LePage (R) beat Matt Dunlap by 5,420 votes. It's the only Democratic seat Republicans flipped in our battleground set.

Also called since our last update: Luna (FL-13), Salazar (FL-27), McGuire (VA-05) and Constantino (NY-21) for Republicans, and Taylor (VA-01), Knickerbocker (OH-10), Lacore (SC-01), Killin (CO-05), Shah (AZ-01) and Mendoza (AZ-06) for Democrats. All match our calls.
news: AP called Mississippi on Nov. 11, about a week after Election Day, once Colom's lead had grown from 1,138 votes to 5,605.
Alaska counts ballots through Nov. 17 and runs the ranked-choice tabulation on Nov. 18.
Louisiana's LA-05 and LA-06 go to Dec. 12 runoffs. Republicans are favored in both.
watch: Alaska Senate: Peltola (D) 121,487, Sullivan (R) 117,512, with 86% counted. That's a 3,975-vote lead with 9,526 votes for others, so the ranked-choice round could matter.
Alaska governor: Kreiss-Tomkins (D) is at 49.8%, just short of a majority. The three Republicans combined trail him. Ranked choice Nov. 18.
Alaska House: Begich (R) is at 49.0% in a four-way race. Ranked choice Nov. 18.

Kansas governor: Holscher (D) leads Masterson by 7,479 with 99% counted. AP hasn't called it, but we called it for Holscher on election night. Kansas has no automatic recount; a candidate can request one at their own cost.
MN-01: Jake Johnson (D) leads Rep. Brad Finstad (R) by 321 votes with 99% counted. That's inside Minnesota's automatic recount range of 0.5%.
